claim: FAO reported on 25 July 2021 that rural livelihoods in Rakhine depended heavily on agriculture, fisheries and aquaculture, while protracted conflict and repeated floods, cyclones and heavy rains disrupted rice production; FAO stated that more than 40% of households in Rakhine were food insecure.
limitations: Regional evidence for Rakhine must not be generalized to all Myanmar. The statement combines chronic conflict vulnerability with recurrent natural hazards and does not isolate causal shares.

claim: The same FAO/EU program rehabilitated 60 fish ponds and built 37 new ponds in Buthidaung and Maungdaw, directly benefiting 97 households as a localized livelihood and food-security stabilizer.
limitations: Very local intervention; should not be interpreted as a national stabilizer or proof of durable recovery.

claim: No sufficiently strong contemporaneous primary source was identified in this batch to quantify diaspora donations or resistance financing before the relevant 2021 cutoffs.
limitations: This is a declared evidence gap, not evidence that such financing did not exist.
